comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Implemented as change https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1669 (commit be915ab89c, stacked on 1662).

PREMISE VERIFIED. _process_start_time reads only /proc/<pid>/stat and returns None on every OSError, so on macOS current_start is always None, the recycled-pid condition is unsatisfiable by construction, and the branch fell to return False with the 1h ceiling explicitly not applied. Unbounded wedge confirmed.

CHANGE. On the live-pid branch, when current_start is None the verdict is unqualified and now takes _mkdir_lock_age_exceeds_ceiling. Corroborated-live (both start times known and equal) still returns False and is never broken on a timer. Known-and-differing still reclaims immediately, independent of age. stamped=None with current known is unchanged.

SAFETY ARGUMENT (recorded, and it is what makes this conservative). _mkdir_lock_is_stale is only reachable from _acquire_mkdir, whose stated precondition is that the caller already holds the exclusive fcntl leg, held for the ENTIRE lifetime of the mkdir leg. A genuinely live owner inside its own hold would still hold that leg, so a reclaimer could not have acquired it and cannot reach this line. Arriving here is itself evidence the stamped owner let go: the ceiling can only fire on an orphan. NOT added: reclaiming on fcntl_held directly, which the same invariant would justify but which widens when a lock may be broken beyond the recorded direction. Left for a follow-up decision.

CONTRACT CHANGE, DELIBERATE. tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py had test_aged_live_pid_with_unknown_start_is_NOT_reclaimed_by_the_ceiling, which pinned the old behaviour and called it 'THE BOUNDARY ... research rec #6, deliberately NOT this change'. That is precisely the gap this bug closes, so the test is inverted with a docstring explaining why, and the module docstring's out-of-scope note updated. It now also asserts a FRESH unqualified-live stamp is still honoured, so the fix reads as adding a bound rather than making the lock instantly reclaimable.

SEAM SPLIT. lock.py was 798/800. Moved the owner-identity/stamp/staleness/reclaim cluster to src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py along the existing call graph: lock.py 510 LOC, lock_owner.py 339 LOC, both inside 200-800, dependency one-way with no cycle.

MIGRATION FINDING worth recording. The plan called for repointing 12 patch sites and 42 attribute sites, which I did. That was not sufficient: lock.py's first cut used 'from lock_owner import <name>', creating a SECOND binding, so monkeypatch on lock_owner did not reach describe_lock_holder and test_describe_never_raises_on_an_unreadable_stamp failed. Fixed by having lock.py reach every moved name module-qualified (_owner.X), leaving exactly one binding. This is the same hazard class as the re-export shim the plan rejected, and is now pinned by test_lock_module_does_not_re_export_the_moved_private_names.

EVIDENCE. 4 new tests (true recycled-pid simulation with a reaped pid and _pid_alive forced True, both fresh-honoured and aged-reclaimed; known-differing-start immediate reclaim; owner-less dir bounded via a forced rmdir failure; the no-shim guard). tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py 10 passed. Full lock suite 76 passed. Wider -k 'lock or store or concur or txn or append': 765 passed, 4 skipped. make lint and make typecheck (510 files) clean.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
[operator-attested] evidence for the two criteria whose proof is a TEST RUN and therefore lives outside the repository.

CHANGE LANDED. Gerrit change 1669 MERGED as 61058f6085 (local be915ab89c, rebased server-side by Rebase-If-Necessary), with LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1. The Verified +1 IS the full-suite pass: CI run https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/31630232865 went green on every job, including pytest on ubuntu-latest py3.11 (13m10s), py3.12 (13m56s), py3.13 (13m20s) and macos-latest py3.13, plus lint + type-check, mutation shards, artifact provenance, optionality, golden-path and verify-identity. macOS matters specifically here: it is the no-/proc platform this bug is about, so that leg exercises the changed branch on the platform where _process_start_time returns None.

CRITERION 1 — the split is behaviour-preserving. Commands run in the worktree with its venv on PATH (env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"):

  python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py tests/unit/test_lock_container_recreate.py tests/unit/test_lock_stale_reclaim.py tests/unit/test_lock_timeout_names_holder_7084.py tests/unit/test_lock_retry_zebrafish.py tests/unit/test_write_lock_busy_probe_7084.py -q
  -> 76 passed in 31.29s

  python -m pytest tests/unit -q -k 'lock or store or concur or txn or append'
  -> 765 passed, 4 skipped in 172.96s

  make lint  -> All checks passed (ruff check + format-check + complexity baseline + zizmor + actionlint)
  make typecheck -> Success: no issues found in 510 source files

Both reference forms were repointed and neither was shimmed. A first cut of the split used 'from lock_owner import <name>' inside lock.py, which created a SECOND binding; monkeypatch on lock_owner then did not reach describe_lock_holder and test_describe_never_raises_on_an_unreadable_stamp FAILED. That failure is the direct evidence that the repoint is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. Fixed by reaching every moved name module-qualified, leaving exactly one binding, and pinned going forward by test_lock_module_does_not_re_export_the_moved_private_names, which asserts the moved names are absent from lock's namespace and present in lock_owner's.

CRITERION 2 — the reported defect no longer reproduces. The reproduction is test_recycled_pid_with_no_proc_is_reclaimed_only_past_the_ceiling in tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py: it stamps a lock with a pid that IS alive but is NOT the process that wrote the stamp (a reaped pid via _dead_pid(), with _pid_alive forced True and _process_start_time forced None to model a platform with no /proc), which is exactly the reported scenario. Under the OLD code _mkdir_lock_is_stale returned False for that stamp at ANY age, which is the unbounded wedge. It now asserts False while fresh and True once aged past _MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S, so the wedge is bounded and the lock is not broken early.

The pre-existing test that PINNED the old behaviour, test_aged_live_pid_with_unknown_start_is_NOT_reclaimed_by_the_ceiling, described itself as 'THE BOUNDARY ... research rec #6, deliberately NOT this change'. That is precisely the gap this bug closes, so it was deliberately inverted, with its docstring and the module docstring rewritten to say why. The inversion of a test that previously encoded the defect is itself end-to-end evidence the behaviour changed.

Not-broken-early is covered by test_aged_live_owner_is_never_reclaimed (corroborated start times, still refused far past the ceiling) and test_recycled_pid_with_a_known_differing_start_is_reclaimed_at_once (proven recycled, reclaimed on evidence rather than a timer).

compiled_state.description:
## Report

Two agents measured the store write lock held ~12 minutes by a process that had ALREADY
EXITED. Investigated under royal-weariless-zebrafish, which REFUTED both an fd leak and
`start=-` defeating liveness.

## Premise verified in current `origin/main` (cc69cc1179)

`src/rebar/_store/lock.py`, `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` (**507**), same-host/same-namespace branch,
lines **565-572**:

```python
if not _pid_alive(pid): return True                                               # 565-566
stamped_start = None if fields["start"] == _STAMP_UNKNOWN else fields["start"]    # 567
current_start = _process_start_time(pid)                                          # 568
if stamped_start is not None and current_start is not None and stamped_start != current_start:
    return True                                     # 569-571  -- recycled-pid discriminator
return False                                        # 572
```

`_process_start_time` (line **265**) reads **only** `/proc/<pid>/stat` (line 273), returning
`None` on every `OSError` (275-276). macOS has no `/proc`, so it ALWAYS returns `None`;
`current_start` at 568 is therefore always `None` there, the line-569 condition is
**unsatisfiable by construction**, and the branch falls to `return False`.

So when the holder is dead but its pid NUMBER was recycled by an unrelated live process,
`_pid_alive` reports "live" and the lock is judged fresh. That branch is deliberately exempt
from the 1h `_MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S` backstop (constant at **107**; exemption documented
in the decision table at **525-531**, "never on a timer alone") because a live pid is treated
as positive proof of liveness. With no start time it is not proof — it is a bare pid-number
collision. Net effect on any platform without `/proc`: an **unbounded** wedge. Recycling is
live on this host (`kern.maxproc: 16000`, already wrapped past the observed stamp pid).

Secondary, already-bounded wedge: `_reclaim_mkdir_lock` removes the owner file then rmdirs,
both best-effort; a failed rmdir leaves an owner-less dir, cleared at the ceiling by the
owner-unreadable branch. Asserted by a test here, not changed.

## Direction (conservative, as recorded)

Apply `_mkdir_lock_age_exceeds_ceiling` on the live-pid branch **only when `current_start` is
unavailable** — only when the "live pid" verdict is unqualified and so not a liveness proof:

* `current_start` known and DIFFERENT from a known `stamped_start` -> reclaim now (unchanged).
* `current_start` known and matching -> `False`, never reclaimed on a timer (unchanged;
  preserves "never break a live owner on a timer alone" wherever `/proc` exists).
* `current_start` is `None` -> unqualified verdict, so fall back to the same 1h ceiling that
  backstops every other unprovable case here. This is the ONLY behaviour change.
* `stamped_start` `None` with `current_start` known -> unchanged `False` (not widened).

**Why the ceiling cannot break a genuinely-live, non-recycled owner.** The worry is a real
owner, alive and holding on a no-`/proc` platform, losing its lock at 1h. The dual-leg
invariant rules it out: `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` is only reached from `_acquire_mkdir` (**602**),
which by its stated precondition runs only AFTER this acquirer took the exclusive
`fcntl.flock` leg, held for the ENTIRE lifetime of the mkdir leg (release order: mkdir, then
fcntl). A live owner inside its hold still holds that fcntl leg, so a reclaimer could not have
acquired it and cannot be at this line at all. Reaching the ceiling check is itself evidence
the stamped owner let go — the orphan case. Blast radius: orphans only.

**Considered and NOT done:** also reclaiming on `fcntl_held` here. The same invariant would
justify reclaiming an orphan at once rather than after an hour, but it widens *when a lock may
be broken* beyond the recorded direction, so it is left for a follow-up decision.

## Module-size seam (required)

`src/rebar/_store/lock.py` is **798** lines against the hard cap of **800**
(`.github/module-size-limit.txt`, CI-enforced), so the fix cannot land without a split. Split
on the existing call-graph seam: extract the owner-identity / stamp / staleness / reclaim
cluster into a new sibling `src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py` —

`_STAMP_UNKNOWN`, `_STAMP_V2_PREFIX`, `_BOOT_ID_PATH`, `_PID_NS_PATH`, `_MKDIR_OWNER_FILE`,
`_MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S`, `_read_boot_id`, `_read_pid_namespace_id`, `_process_start_time`,
`_host_identity`, `_owner_stamp`, `_parse_v2_stamp`, `_describe_stamped_pid`,
`_mkdir_lock_age_s`, `_mkdir_lock_age_exceeds_ceiling`, `_pid_alive`, `_legacy_stamp_is_stale`,
`_mkdir_lock_is_stale`, `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`

— leaving `lock.py` with the fcntl leg, `_acquire_mkdir`, `LockHandle`, and the
`acquire`/`write_lock` API. The cluster is 270 LOC, so `lock_owner.py` lands near 290 (with
header and imports) and `lock.py` near 548: both inside the 200-800 band, no file under 100.

The dependency runs **one way, `lock.py` -> `lock_owner.py`**, no cycle. It is NOT the case
that nothing left behind references the cluster: `_acquire_mkdir` calls `_owner_stamp`,
`_mkdir_lock_is_stale`, `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`, and the two public reporters that stay —
`write_lock_is_busy` (**333**) and `describe_lock_holder` (**383**) — reach `_parse_v2_stamp`,
`_describe_stamped_pid`, `_mkdir_lock_age_s`, `_MKDIR_OWNER_FILE`. All become imports from
`lock_owner`; nothing in `lock_owner` imports `lock`.

**Migration detail — BOTH reference forms, not just patches.** A sweep of the 4 affected test
modules found:

* **12 string-form `monkeypatch.setattr` sites** over `_read_boot_id`,
  `_read_pid_namespace_id`, `_process_start_time`, `_pid_alive`, `_parse_v2_stamp`, plus 2
  patching `_lock.socket.gethostname` (read by `_host_identity`).
* **42 plain attribute-access sites** on the `from rebar._store import lock as _lock` binding
  — the larger half, breaking identically: `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` (17), `_owner_stamp` (13),
  `_MKDIR_OWNER_FILE` (5), `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`, `_host_identity`,
  `_MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S` (1 each) — over `test_lock_age_ceiling.py` (14),
  `test_lock_container_recreate.py` (15), `test_lock_stale_reclaim.py` (9),
  `test_lock_timeout_names_holder_7084.py` (4).

A re-export shim would keep the attribute half green while **silently breaking the patch
half**: the moved `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` resolves patched names through its OWN module
globals, so a shim would leave those tests asserting nothing. No shim — every site of either
form is repointed at `lock_owner`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A dead holder whose pid was recycled by an unrelated live process is reclaimed once past
      the ceiling where `_process_start_time` returns `None` — test stamps a lock with a
      live-but-unrelated pid, forces no start time, asserts stale past the ceiling and NOT
      before it
- [x] A live holder whose stamped and current start times both exist and MATCH is never
      reclaimed however old the lock — test asserts refusal well past the ceiling
- [x] A live pid whose known start time DIFFERS from the stamp is still reclaimed at once,
      independent of age — test (regression guard on the existing branch)
- [x] The owner-less-dir path is bounded by the ceiling — test removes the owner file and
      asserts stale only past it
- [x] `lock.py` and `lock_owner.py` are each within `.github/module-size-limit.txt` and no new
      file is under 100 LOC — verified against `git archive HEAD`
- [x] The split is behaviour-preserving: every pre-existing lock test passes with BOTH
      reference forms repointed to `lock_owner` (12 patch-string, 42 attribute-access), and
      `rebar._store.lock` carries no re-export shim for any moved name — test asserts the
      moved names are absent from `lock`'s namespace [operator-attested]
- [x] The reported defect no longer reproduces: a recycled pid on a platform without `/proc`
      is reclaimed rather than wedging the store unboundedly [operator-attested]

file_impact.reason: seam split; retains fcntl leg, _acquire_mkdir, LockHandle, acquire/write_lock
new module: owner stamp identity, staleness adjudication, reclaim; ceiling applied when start time unavailable
recycled-pid reclamation tests; patch targets repointed

compiled_state.title: Stale mkdir lock is UNBOUNDED on platforms without /proc: recycled pid defeats reclamation
